text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London rebounded from the early losses to end higher after a muted session. July added $5 to close at $1,765 per tonne, while September closed $14 higher at $1,797 per tonne. Activity was dominated by July/September switches as players rolled forward the July positions before the contract's first tender day on Tuesday. The market noted USDA's downward revision in Indonesia's 1997/98 coffee crop to 4.6 million bags from 6.1 million bags previously.

Arabica futures in New York ended higher on news of cold weather in Brazil. July closed 2.50 cents/lb higher at 192.40 cents/lb. September added 3.10 cents/lb to close at 172.40 cents/lb. The deferreds closed between 1.90 and 3.50 cents/lb higher. The July/September switch narrowed to 20.00 cents/lb from 20.60 cents/lb at the close on Friday, while the September/December switch widened to 21.50 cents/lb compared with 20.30 cents/lb. Brazilian meteorologists Somar said that a polar air mass may pass through Brazil's coffee growing regions from the evening of July 5, representing the greatest threat of frost seen so far this year. But US forecaster Weather Services Corporation said that no damaging cold is indicated as a warm, high pressure dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to remain basically unchanged for the next seven days. PHILIPPINES - Philippine coffee production in 1997/98 (July/June) is forecast to rise to 984,000 bags (935,000 bags robustas and 49,000 bags arabicas), up from 937,000 bags (890,000 bags robustas and 47,000 bags arabicas) produced in 1996/97. Production in 1995/96 reached 875,000 bags (833,000 bags robustas and 42,000 bags arabicas).

BRAZIL - The Brazilian government's coffee auction, scheduled to be held on July 2, is now expected to take place on July 9 due to a change in auction rules. According to the president of the Sao Paulo Coffee Industry Union the change involves an extension in payment terms to 120 from 60 days, approved recently by the country's National Monetary Council. Although no quantity has so far been set, the sale is likely to be for around 300,000 60-kg bags, it was added.

AUSTRIA - Coffee imports in calendar year 1996 reached 1.208 million 60-kg bags, 2 percent less than was imported the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Kenya (83,100 vs 14,200 bags), Honduras (90,600 vs 87,000 bags), Brazil (132,800 vs 113,900 bags) and Colombia (103,700 vs 92,100 bags).
The country exported 162,000 bags of coffee in 1996, sharply down on last year's figure of 228,700 bags.
